title: The Finite-Prefix Indeterminacy Theorem for the Two-Point Liouville Correlation
summary: Let \lambda(n) = (-1)^{\Omega(n)} be the Liouville function, \Omega the number of prime factors counted with multiplicity, and let \mathrm{corr}(h,N) = \sum_{n=1}^{N} \lambda(n)\lambda(n+h). The two-point Chowla conjecture in the case h = 2 asserts \mathrm{corr}(2,N) = o(N); it is open. We prove that it is also not decidable from finite data. Explicitly, for each index a let \lambda_a be \lambda with its value at a negated. Then \lambda_a(n) = \lambda(n) for every n < a; consequently \mathrm{corrSlice}(h,a,N) = \mathrm{corr}(h,N) whenever N + h < a, so the two functions present identical correlation data on every prefix shorter than a, while \lambda_a \ne \lambda.
